text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks in the Strait of Hormuz this week, pushing U.S. crude toward $102 a barrel and Brent crude to $110—a meaningful move for an oil producer whose revenue rises directly with the price of oil it sells. The stock has climbed 15.6% over two weeks as these regional risks have mounted.

Beyond today's headline, the broader backdrop matters: tanker rates have surged enough to add roughly $38 per barrel to the true cost of delivering physical oil, according to energy analysts, which can squeeze some competitors while benefiting large integrated producers like ConocoPhillips that manage their own supply chains. Meanwhile, the gap between U.S. oil ($101.91) and world oil ($126.55) has widened considerably, reflecting supply concerns tied to the Strait of Hormuz disruptions—exactly the kind of dislocation that rewards companies with diversified production and refining assets.
